claims.statement: create_chess_agent builds on create_agent with no tools and a fixed stack order: ChessCore first, then ForcedMoveMiddleware (unless forced_move=False), then each user middleware wrapped by guard(), then a summarization node (ChessSummarization when memory=True, or NoSummarization when memory=False with fixed_topology=True), and always StallRetry last.
With model=None the agent uses a NoModel stand-in whose invocation raises ChessContractError, so a System-1-only agent fails loudly instead of playing a random move when no middleware proposes.
create_chess_agent rejects at build time two extensions declaring the same private state key, and any compiled input schema exposing keys other than messages and position.
ChessCore.before_agent classifies each run as execute, reject or noop; reject and noop jump straight to end, and only execute runs are finalized by after_agent.

A run carrying both a position and a new human message is rejected; once outcome is set any command is rejected as 'the game is over' and an empty run is a noop, checked before any sync because a resignation cannot be rederived from the board.

The request key is a position fingerprint (SHA-256 of start_fen, moves and sorted restrict) or the chat message id; repeating the last turn's request retries it if pending and is a noop otherwise, and a run with no command retries a pending turn or is a noop.

A new chat message (other than a resign or draw control command) while a turn is pending is rejected ('finish or retry the pending turn first'), while a new valid position command marks the pending turn abandoned (folding extension turn_calls and turn_latency_ms into it) and opens a new turn.
Rejected commands write the reason to error and remove the offending chat message from messages, without touching the game record.

Chat input must be exactly 'go', one legal move in SAN or UCI, or a control command ('resign <side>' / 'draw <side>', handled before sync); position input must keep the thread's root and extend its moves as a prefix, with a non-empty legal restrict, and new moves are recorded as external plies.

When a turn opens, initial_allowed is set to the legal moves filtered by restrict; if the synced position has already ended, the turn is opened directly as terminal with the outcome and a result message, and the run is a noop without calling the model.

Retrying a pending turn that already holds a validated proposal or terminal_intent jumps straight to end for finalization instead of calling the model again; otherwise the retry resets decision keys and restores allowed_moves to initial_allowed.

Extension before_model hooks must be idempotent because an illegal-reply retry re-enters at the first before_model; decisions should be frozen per turn_id and replayed as current allowed intersected with the frozen set.

ChessCore.wrap_model_call replaces the request messages with model_view output plus a trailing, never-stored position message, records provider calls into the turn's calls, and accumulates wrapper wall time into turn.latency_ms.

model_view with memory=False shows only the current turn from its opening message; with memory=True it drops earlier turns' rejected attempts and feedback; in both it shows only the current turn's latest rejected reply (keeping its reasoning blocks), strips reasoning blocks from other AI messages, and returns deep copies.

Empty AI replies are stored as the '[no text in reply]' placeholder because Anthropic rejects replayed assistant turns without text, and the feedback tells the model its output budget was probably spent on reasoning.

Provider exceptions whose text matches context-overflow hints are converted by errors.provider_errors to ContextBudgetError (raised directly, or re-raised by after_model when calls had already completed), and the turn remains pending.

parse_move reads only the last case-insensitive MOVE: marker's line (rejecting an empty last marker rather than falling back to an earlier one), uses the last move-like token only when no marker exists, and tries SAN then UCI requiring legality.

A legal move that is not in allowed_moves, or no move, counts as an illegal attempt: feedback is appended and the run jumps back to model while the prior illegal_attempts count is below max_retries; after that a resignation terminal_intent with reason illegal_moves (a forfeit) is set for the side to move (four illegal replies with the default max_retries=3).

ForcedMoveMiddleware proposes the single move and skips the model only when the turn's initial_allowed has exactly one move and no proposal exists, deliberately ignoring allowed_moves and candidates so narrowing is never mistaken for a forced position.

after_agent finalizes atomically: a terminal_intent makes the turn terminal with the outcome; a proposal is revalidated against legal and allowed moves (else ChessContractError), appended as a ply with source, analysis, model, turn_id, latency and extension ply_meta, and the turn is marked committed; a missing proposal and intent is a ChessContractError.
After committing a move, ending() is checked on the new board and outcome is written in the same update, so a game-ending agent move leaves its turn committed rather than terminal.

ending() always applies automatic endings (checkmate, stalemate, insufficient material, fivefold, 75-move) and, only with draw_claims='auto', a threefold repetition or fifty-move rule that has actually occurred, never a draw merely claimable by the next move.
replay rebuilds from the root and checks for an ending before every ply, so positions containing moves after the game ended are rejected as CommandError.
turn.latency_ms, copied onto the ply, is the time inside ChessCore.wrap_model_call plus each extension's turn_latency_ms added once when the turn finalizes (System 1 reports its frozen ranking time).

fixed_topology=True keeps a summarization node under memory=False via NoSummarization, a no-op before_model with the same SummarizationMiddleware node name, so graphs for both memory settings share one topology; it does not affect ForcedMoveMiddleware, which forced_move=False still removes.

The Agent Server always builds the chess graph with fixed_topology=True and GameSetupMiddleware, and build_agent then always includes a System 1 node (NoSystemOne when the policy is llm); the model-free shape() graph used for reads and introspection is built with NoSystemOne, GameSetupMiddleware and fixed_topology=True, so it matches the running graph.

Each run writes a fresh private invocation {id, action, opened_turn}; opened_turn names the turn this run opened (pending or opened directly as terminal) and is None for retries, rejects and ordinary noops.

GameSetupMiddleware writes the thread's setup only when there is exactly one turn whose id equals invocation.opened_turn, checking in both before_agent and after_agent because a run opening a terminal turn jumps from ChessCore.before_agent past the extension's before_agent.
illegal_attempts is counted on the durable TurnRecord rather than in the reset decision keys, so a retry after a provider error keeps the illegal-move budget.

If a model call fails after some provider calls completed, ChessCore.wrap_model_call keeps those calls on the turn and sets a failed_call marker; after_model re-raises the remembered exception in the same run, and on a later resume (exception no longer in memory) clears the marker and jumps back to model.

StallRetry is a core-owned ModelRetryMiddleware appended last in every chess agent's stack, so as the innermost model-call wrapper it repeats only the provider call inside the same turn, and it adds no graph node.
StallRetry retries only langchain_openai's StreamChunkTimeoutError (nothing when langchain_openai is not installed), at most once and with no delay; any other error fails the turn immediately.
StallRetry uses on_failure='error', so a second stall re-raises instead of becoming the model's reply; the run fails with the turn still pending and an empty retry resumes the same turn.
A stalled attempt records no call on the turn: a turn that stalls once then succeeds has one recorded call and an unchanged illegal_attempts count.
create_chess_agent defaults draw_claims to 'auto', while the UCI adapter forces draw_claims='never' because the GUI adjudicates draws.

The trailing position message always includes the moves so far, a custom starting FEN, the side to move, check, the permitted moves on a restricted turn and the MOVE request; the renderer (show_fen, show_board, move_list, or a custom render_position) supplies only the position and move-list sections.

A provider 400 error about the reasoning effort (param reasoning.effort or reasoning_effort, or effort mentioned in the text when no param is given) is translated to ReasoningEffortError advising removal of the effort setting, and the turn remains pending.

A 'resign <side>' chat command, accepted for either side on either side's move and checked before the pending-turn rejection, abandons any pending turn and discards its saved proposal or forfeit, opens a terminal turn with a resignation outcome (reason 'resigned', winner the other side), and runs as a noop without calling the model.

A 'draw <side>' offer opens no turn: it is rejected while a turn is pending, off the offering side's move, or when repeated by that side in the same position; otherwise the draw_policy's answer is appended to draw_offers as {ply, by, answer} and the run is a noop. create_chess_agent does not expose draw_policy, so factory-built agents use decline_all.

Control commands must name the side ('resign white' or 'draw black', case-insensitive, single-spaced) because the server does not know which side is human; a known verb with an unknown side is rejected as a CommandError.
